decisive_items: Repeat lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 30 cm H₂O, 1762 WBCs/mm³ (60% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 123 mg/dL, glucose 30 mg/dL (serum 105 mg/dL)
new involvement of the left basal ganglia, increased diffusion restriction, development of necrosis, and new peripheral contrast enhancement
response.rationale: The clinical picture of fever, leukocytosis, CSF polymorphonuclear pleocytosis with low glucose, and imaging progression from a mass-like lesion to necrosis with ring enhancement is most consistent with pyogenic brain abscess. Negative Gram stain is explained by prior antibiotics or fastidious organisms. Other candidates lack key features: endocarditis is excluded by negative echocardiography; PML classically lacks fever and CSF PMN pleocytosis; toxoplasmosis typically has lymphocytic CSF and ring enhancement earlier; rickettsial and vasculitis are not supported by CSF profile and negative studies.

rejected.why: No valvular vegetations on echocardiography; presentation not typical for endocarditis alone.
Same as R2; embolic infarcts less likely without vegetations.
Rickettsial studies negative; CSF profile more bacterial than rickettsial.
Lack of typical ring enhancement until late, PMN-predominant CSF, and no HIV mention.
Negative JC virus PCR, fever, leukocytosis, and PMN pleocytosis are atypical for PML.
Vasculitis would not produce abscess-like CSF findings and ring enhancement.
